root_cause.text: The driver allocated the control message buffer using devm_kzalloc() with the parent USB device (&udev->dev) instead of the USB interface device (&intf->dev), causing the buffer's lifetime to be tied to the USB device rather than the driver's binding, leading to a memory leak when the driver is unbound without the USB device being physically disconnected.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `devm_kzalloc(&udev->dev, ...)` to `devm_kzalloc(&intf->dev, ...)`, and the commit message explicitly states that USB drivers should have their managed resources tied to the interface device to avoid memory leaks on driver unbind (e.g., probe deferral or configuration changes). The fix ensures the buffer is released when the driver unbinds from the interface.

    adapters from Theobroma Systems. There are two form-factors
    that run essentially the same firmware:
    
    * Seal: standalone USB stick ( https://www.theobroma-systems.com/seal )

bic_trace_step.reason: In ucan_probe(), line 'ctl_msg_buffer = devm_kzalloc(&udev->dev, sizeof(union ucan_ctl_payload), GFP_KERNEL);' uses &udev->dev (parent USB device) instead of &intf->dev (USB interface device).
